name: Packages
summary: Keeps your parcels in one place: each one's status and last event, checked for you on a schedule, with a card on your Bench when one arrives or runs into trouble.
author: The JimmyHQ project

secrets.name: seventeentrack_key
secrets.label: 17TRACK security key
secrets.help: From the Settings page of your 17TRACK API account. Only used when the tracking service below is 17TRACK.

settings.label: Tracking service
settings.help: Practice looks nothing up: you set each status by hand, which is a way to try Packages out. 17TRACK looks parcels up for you, and needs its key below and a 17TRACK account.

settings.label: Check every (hours)
settings.help: How long after one check the next one is made. Press Refresh now to check sooner.

settings.label: Also check every day at
settings.help: A time in your own time zone on a 24-hour clock, such as 06:00, so there is news waiting in the morning. Leave it empty for no daily check.

settings.label: Try again after a failed check (minutes)
settings.help: When a check gets no clear answer, nothing is changed and Packages tries again after this long. Each failure in a row doubles the wait, up to the longest wait below.

settings.label: Longest wait between tries (minutes)
settings.help: The most the wait after failed checks grows to.

settings.label: Least time between checks from Refresh now (minutes)
settings.help: A tracking service counts what it is asked, so Refresh now waits at least this long after the last check. 0 means no wait.

settings.label: Stop checking a delivered package after (days)
settings.help: A delivered package stays in Delivered, and is checked until then in case the carrier corrects itself.

settings.label: Stop checking a package with no news after (days)
settings.help: 17TRACK stops tracking a number its carrier has said nothing new about for 30 days. Packages stops checking such a package too, and says so on it. 0 means never.

settings.label: Tell me when a package
settings.help: Packages puts a card on your Bench, once for each change, with the package's name and no tracking number.

options.label: Is delivered or has a problem

settings.label: Numbers asked about at once
settings.help: The most tracking numbers sent in one request. A tracking service may take fewer: Packages never sends more than it takes.

settings.label: Call a new package "not found" after (hours)
settings.help: A carrier often does not know a number for a while after a label is made. Until then a new package reads as waiting for the carrier. 0 means at once.

settings.label: Wait for the tracking service for (seconds)
settings.help: How long one request may take before it counts as no answer.

settings.label: Look at the schedule every (minutes)
settings.help: How often Packages asks itself whether a check is due. It does not ask the tracking service.

settings.label: Pause between requests (milliseconds)
settings.help: 17TRACK allows 3 requests a second; a check of many packages waits this long between its requests.

settings.label: Practice: minutes until a package is delivered
settings.help: Only with the Practice tracking service, which looks nothing up. A package you add moves by itself from waiting to on its way, out for delivery and delivered, taking about this long, so you can see Packages and its card on your Bench at work. A package whose status you set yourself is left alone.

settings.label: Packages on the screen
settings.help: How many packages the screen lists.
